tools.name: find_manuals
tools.description:
Find the service manual for a car. Accepts how people describe it: brand, model name, year,
chassis code, engine or transmission code, e.g. "2004 Sentra 1.8", "B15", "QG18DE", "Mazda 3".
Returns manuals best match first, factory service manuals before owner's manuals; pass a
result's 'manual' to sea

tools.name: get_contents
tools.description:
List the files (sections) of a manual with what each covers, page counts and links.
With 'file' (its full path, or its name within 'manual'), list that file's bookmarks (its own
table of contents) instead.

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Look up components, systems and jobs in one car's manual index, e.g. "timing chain",
"camshaft position sensor", "a/t fluid", "spark plug", "brake caliper". 'manual' is required:
a manual from find_manuals, or its model folder to cover all years. The query is split into the
manual's index terms; pag

tools.name: lookup_dtc
tools.description:
Look up a diagnostic trouble code (P0340, C1105, U1000, or an old Nissan blink code like 34)
in one car's manual and return where its diagnosis starts: page, title, and the parent bookmarks
('within'). A manual covering several engines or systems has one diagnosis per variant, so check
'within' (e.g

tools.name: read_pages
tools.description: Read the text of 'count' pages (max 6) of a file, starting at 'page' (1-based).

tools.name: page_image
tools.description:
Render one PDF page as a PNG image: use it for wiring diagrams, connector pin views,
exploded views and tables that read poorly as text. Returns a short text part first (the page
link, its heading and text) and then the image. If no image reaches you, your client does not
pass images on: use the tex

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: find_manuals · Private data: find_manuals, get_contents, read_pages, page_image · Public sink: find_manuals · Destructive: find_manuals, page_image.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: find_manuals · Private data: find_manuals, get_contents, read_pages, page_image · Public sink: find_manuals · Destructive: find_manuals, page_image

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
